chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Ali ibn Rashid, who said:

I asked him, saying: 'May I be your ransom, a man purchased goods for a thousand dirhams or thereabouts, and did not specify the dirhams clearly, nor anything else.' He said: 'If he stipulated [a specific type] upon you, then his stipulation applies; otherwise, the dirhams of the people that are acceptable among them [apply].'

He said: 'And I meant by that [the question] to know what is obligatory upon me regarding the dowry, because they said: We do not accept except a clear [specified] amount, and I only married upon specified dirhams, and we did not say

key_terms.دَرَاهِمُ اَلنَّاسِ: the dirhams of the people (standard circulating currency)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a currency is not clearly specified in a contract or dowry?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of 'urf' (customary practice) in Islamic jurisprudence, ruling that unspecified monetary obligations default to the standard circulating currency rather than requiring explicit numerical specification. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical commercial norms, clarifying that the validity of contracts like marriage (nikah) relies on the mutual understanding of the prevailing medium of exchange. This ruling resolves disputes where parties might otherwise argue over technicalities of currency naming versus actual value.
